text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: High error rate detected on /v1/generate (canary rollout). Aggregate 5xx rate 18% over 5m, latency spikes in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Pager triggered to oncall.
oncall-bot: Incident ID INC-2398765432. Severity: P1. Initial triage channel: #incidents.
ops_pager: paging mike.h (oncall)
mike.h: I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xx and repeated "variant_mismatch" logs from router.
jess.k: oncall-sre joining. any customer-facing impact yet?
sara_ops: CS reporting increased error rate for Checkout API on a few customers, some saw timeouts. flagged 2 enterprise tenants.
lee: digging into smart-routing logs now — looks like canary variant v2 was supposed to get 5% traffic, but I see routing policy falling back repeatedly from v2 -> v1 -> v2 across region handoffs. loop pattern every ~10s.
product-ml: that sounds like sticky fallback TTL + compatibility mismatch. v2 was rolled with new tokenizer change, but rollout policy allowed fallback to v1 and sticky affinity left enabled.
eng-sre: confirmed: fallback policy has sticky_affinity: true and ttl_seconds: 3600. When v2 returns 5xx, router selects fallback v1 but marks affinity to v1; when v1 hits a model-variant-tag check it fails (model_arch mismatch) and falls back to v2, creating oscillation.
mike.h: can someone grep for "sticky_affinity" in the active policy bundle?
lee: found policy: 
```
{"policy_id": "policy-rc-22", "strategy": "canary", "canary_pct": 5, "fallback": {"behavior": "sticky", "ttl_seconds": 3600}}
```
ops_pager: copying logs: router shows repeated "variant_compat_check_failed: tokenizer_mismatch" entries. timestamped loops across eu and us regions.
jess.k: This explains region fallback loops too — sticky affinity is global so session pins across regions despite regional capacity gaps.
cs_lead: prioritizing customer comms. Which tenants impacted?
sara_ops: Tenant IDs t-452 and t-909. Both using long-context feature; saw increased latency + 502s.
product-ml: Root cause hypothesis: v2 was onboarded without proper compatibility flag (tokenizer version mismatched). Routing policy allowed sticky fallback which made oscillation persistent.
mike.h: escalation: we need a live mitigation ASAP. Options: 1) Pause the canary rollout 2) Flip fallback to non-sticky (best) 3) Reduce TTL to 0 or clear affinity cache 4) Force-rollback v2 to v1.
jess.k: I can run a quick policy change to non-sticky fallback. that should stop oscillation and allow deterministic fallback to stable. downside: some sessions may failover more often but better than loop.
lee: also recommend evicting session-affinity cache entries for the affected tenants/regions. command: `redwood routing affinity evict --tenant t-452,t-909 --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1`
eng-sre: prepared a playbook snippet to pause rollout: `redwood rollout pause --id rollout-202-rc22`
mike.h: execute non-sticky change first — less customer-visible. jess.k, proceed and confirm. I'll notify CS and product.
jess.k: running: `redwood policy update --id policy-rc-22 --fallback.behavior=non-sticky`
jess.k: (output) OK — policy updated, propagation to control plane started.
eng-sre: propagate confirmed on control plane. pushing to region routers now.
lee: running affinity evict for the two tenants.
lee: (output) evict OK, cache cleared for listed tenants in eu-west-1, us-east-1.
ops_pager: monitoring metrics.
mike.h: metrics update?
ops_pager: 2m post-change error rate down to 4.5% cluster-wide, eu-west1 still at 7% but trending down. latency stable.
sara_ops: CS — notifying affected customers that we mitigated and are investigating root cause. drafting message now.
cs_lead: please include ETA for fix and if we plan rollback.
product-ml: we should still pause the canary to avoid further exposure while we fix tokenizer mismatch. I'll request rollback.
mike.h: go ahead and pause. eng-sre, execute pause command.
eng-sre: `redwood rollout pause --id rollout-202-rc22` -> OK. canary paused.
jess.k: double-check routing policies — new policy now non-sticky, ttl unchanged but affinity entries cleared.
lee: verified routers no longer issuing repeated variant switches. no loop traces in logs for last 3m.
ops_pager: error rate now 1.2% and trending to baseline.
product-ml: plan: 1) Rollback v2 build from canary, 2) fix tokenizer compatibility in the model packaging, 3) add automated compatibility checks to onboarding pipeline, 4) change default fallback behavior for canaries to non-sticky for next 30 days.
mike.h: assign owners and ETA.
product-ml: owners: model packaging fix -> product-ml (jess.k + lee), pipeline check -> eng-runtime (eng-sre), policy default change -> product (product-ml). ETA 48 hours for full fix, but we will re-run canary only after sign-off.
sara_ops: CS update: sent interim message to affected tenants, offered workaround and apology.
cs_lead: also temp credits? we'll handle via support.
eng-sre: creating incident page and postmortem. adding logs and commands used.
ops_pager: creating oncall handoff note — today's oncall (mike.h) will hand to next shift at 0700 UTC, but if error rate resurges escalate immediately.
mike.h: acknowledged. leaving a brief summary for next oncall.
product-ml: follow-ups: add preflight compat check in model onboarding, tighten canary fallback defaults, add detection for oscillation (>=3 variant swaps in 60s).
jess.k: adding a realtime alert rule: if variant_swap_rate > 3/min then auto-disable sticky fallback for that route.
lee: also recommend reducing TTL for sticky fallback to 60s by default.
eng-sre: documented commands used: 
```
redwood policy update --id policy-rc-22 --fallback.behavior=non-sticky
redwood rollout pause --id rollout-202-rc22
redwood routing affinity evict --tenant t-452,t-909 --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1
```
mike.h: closing notes: mitigation successful, canary paused, customer impact contained to two tenants with CS notified. Postmortem to be drafted and linked here.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2398765432 status -> mitigated (P1 -> P2) at 2398765860. Postmortem assigned to eng-sre/product-ml.
eng-sre: I'll start the postmortem and ping owners for details.
product-ml: thanks team.
cs_lead: marking ticket for follow-up with legal for enterprise SLA impact review.
mike.h: thanks all, handing off to night oncall.
